findings.evidence: Common mistakes row 'Not redirecting `inventory` to a file | It prints JSON to stdout only' repeats step 1's own command `> "$WORK/inventory.json"` and the NEVER list (hand-write, --force, dry run) is restated again in the table
findings.fix: Drop the Common mistakes rows that only repeat a step command or a NEVER item (inventory redirect, apply while needs_choice remains, dry run and apply in one turn), and keep the rows that add a new failure cause (agent_skills JSON list, approve_with edited, restore after committed apply)

findings.evidence: Step 3 packs runner models, the pi steer, trusted roots, execution, --force and removals into one 50-line sub-list under '3. **Review the plan with the user**'
findings.fix: Split step 3 into a short checkpoint (resolve every needs_choice, then list each unset with its existing value) and move the per-key rules (pi steer, trusted roots, runner model and router_backed) into a 'Plan keys' table that step 3 points to, so the Process pattern keeps clear phases and checkpoints

findings.evidence: Gotchas that defy assumptions (PI_PROVIDER only in the pi bash tool, opencode bare profile still loading ~/.agents/skills) are spread across the Scope, steps and Cross-AI sections, not in one Gotchas list
findings.fix: Add a short '## Gotchas' list before NEVER that collects the environment facts: PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL are set only in the pi agent's bash tool; the opencode bare profile still loads ~/.agents/skills; the v2 hook runs codex unsandboxed; the dry run does not check the apply marker

findings.evidence: Description spends words on internals ('v2 flow — inventory, recommend, plan edits, apply, follow-ups; the kept v1 path asks only `model_profile`') and has no explicit 'Not for' boundary next to its neighbours (gsd-settings tuning, running GSD phases, ai-kit-cross-ai dispatch)
findings.fix: Curated GSD `.planning/config.json` setup for a target project: picks models per tier, wires installed skills to GSD agents, and sets up cross-AI plan review and a cross-AI execution runner (cross-ai.mjs). Use when asked to configure or migrate .planning/config.json, set up GSD config fast, wire skills to GSD agents, choose the pi session steer, render cross-ai.mjs, run ensure-runner or merge a cross-ai.mjs.new, even without naming GSD settings. A faster alternative to gsd-settings/gsd-config, not a replacement. Not for advanced GSD tuning (gsd-settings --advanced), running GSD phases, or dispatching a cross-AI call (ai-kit-cross-ai).

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 409 lines but about 4,250 words (well over the ~5,000-token body budget); the Skills section (lines 273-327), the Limits table and the runner exit-code paragraph load on every run
findings.fix: Move the Skills wiring and refusal rules into references/skills-wiring.md, read when a plan has an agent_skills or trusted-root entry or a skill_unwired note; move the runner exit-code list to references/runner.md (already gated on a non-ok AIKIT-XAI status), so the body stays under ~5,000 tokens

findings.evidence: 'rigor: `mvp` ..., `standard` ..., or `rigorous` ...' and 'cross-AI plan review: y / n / default' give the user equal options with no recommended rigor, unlike model_profile, which says 'adaptive recommended'
findings.fix: Name a default rigor in step 2 (for example 'standard recommended') and say that 'default' is the recommended answer for both cross-AI questions unless the user has a reason, so the menus get a default the way model_profile already does

findings.evidence: 16 queries (8/8); most negatives share no keyword with the skill ('explain how the Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaler', 'write a README for my personal dotfiles'), and there is no near-miss for gsd-settings --advanced tuning or for dispatching a cross-AI call
findings.fix: Bring it to about 20 queries and replace the weak negatives with near-misses: 'open gsd-settings --advanced and tune dynamic_routing', 'run a cross-AI review of this plan with codex now', 'execute phase 3 with the cross-ai runner', 'edit opencode.jsonc to add a provider'

findings.evidence: Assertions are vague or conflict with the skill: 'The answer renders the runner through the cross-AI build step' (no such step in SKILL.md); 'asks only the choices it cannot resolve itself' while SKILL.md step 2 mandates exactly four questions; only one eval has an input file
findings.fix: Rewrite them as checkable statements tied to SKILL.md: 'asks exactly the four questions of step 2 in one message', 'the plan sets workflow.cross_ai_command to node .planning/scripts/cross-ai.mjs', 'lists each unset row with its existing value'; add inventory.json/plan.json fixtures under evals/files/ for the plan-review and dry-run evals

findings.evidence: Step 3 says a trusted-root decline is 'refused while agents still hold the skills it covers — the full rule is in Skills', a forward reference 130 lines down; the runner exit-code paragraph (lines 44-50) is one dense run-on sentence that is hard to act on
findings.fix: Put the decline action inline in step 3 ('declining means plan-set agent_skills.<agent> without those skills, as the refusal prints') and turn the runner exit codes into a two-column table (exit, statuses) in references/runner.md, linked from the step that reads AIKIT-XAI

findings.evidence: Before the first command the skill asks 'Was its config last written by v1 ...' but gives no branch for what to do when the answer is yes, beyond the long parenthetical
findings.fix: Add an explicit branch: 'If yes, run the v2 flow anyway and, in step 3, name every v1 override the unset rows remove; never run apply-execution afterwards'
